causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: At 3.45 am Pelican Point power station tripped, meaning around 240 MW of capacity, priced below $100/MWh, was no longer available.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Following the trip at Pelican Point, imports from Victoria were reduced by 240 MW. Imports were reduced to protect the power system in South Australia, in case the Heywood interconnector also tripped.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Of the 1,750 MW of semi-scheduled wind installed, less than 200 MW was available due to calm weather conditions.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: The reduced availability was due to some older gas plant at Torrens Island and Osborne not offering their capacity along with low wind conditions and no solar, as the event was before dawn.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: While the capacity that started (received a target) made up for the lost generation at Pelican Point, this capacity was either priced at the cap or could not set price as it was ramp constrained, technically constrained or at max capacity.

constraints_named.id: constraint that manages the import limit into South Australia
constraints_named.quote: A constraint that manages the import limit into South Australia uses the number of thermal units that are currently generating locally to calculate the amount of electricity that South Australia can safely import without risking the stability of the power system.

constraints_named.id: constraint protecting the stability of the power system in South Australia
constraints_named.quote: A constraint protecting the stability of the power system in South Australia was setting the import limit throughout the day.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood
interconnectors_named.quote: Following the trip at Pelican Point, imports from Victoria were reduced by 240 MW. Imports were reduced to protect the power system in South Australia, in case the Heywood interconnector also tripped.

interconnectors_named.name: Murraylink
interconnectors_named.quote: South Australia is connected to Victoria via two interconnectors, Heywood and Murraylink.

intervals.quote: On 22 January 2021 the spot price in South Australia reached $5,031/MWh for the 4 am trading interval.

peak_price.quote: On 22 January 2021 the spot price in South Australia reached $5,031/MWh for the 4 am trading interval.

rebid_set_price.quote: Generator rebidding from prices below to above $5,000/MWh did not contribute to the 4 am price outcome.
